critical_code_review_comments: _public_cors middleware (server.py L6581) is correctly registered AFTER add_middleware(CORSMiddleware,...), so in Starlette's reversed middleware stack it runs FIRST and short-circuits preflights before the restrictive CORSMiddleware can reject them. Good design.
Vary: Origin is set, which prevents intermediaries from caching wrong-origin responses. Good.

Echoing the raw Origin in Access-Control-Allow-Origin is acceptable for public endpoints (these are unauthenticated, read/write to public card slugs only) and necessary because the widget runs on arbitrary client domains. No credentialed CSRF surface is exposed via /api/public/*.

Minor: middleware also sets header on non-OPTIONS responses with origin fallback '*' when no Origin header present — fine, but could log unusual server-to-server callers for observability if leads spike.

rca of the issue: Original prod issue ('Ups, no pude responder' on external client sites): the widget loaded from ezunitech.com makes a cross-origin POST to /api/public/card/{slug}/chat. With a restrictive CORS_ORIGINS list, FastAPI's CORSMiddleware rejected the preflight with HTTP 400 and no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so the browser blocked the actual POST and embed.js fell back to its error string. Fix (verified): a custom @app.middleware('http') named _public_cors intercepts /api/public/* requests, returns 200 on OPTIONS with Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing the caller's Origin (+ Vary: Origin), and appends the same header to actual responses. Verified by curling localhost:8001 directly with Origin: https://some-external-client.com and by browser flow on /embed-test.html.
